values: Verify that an admin account is successfully created when all fields contain valid data meeting the criteria.

1. The LoadTrack signup page (loadtrack-gamma.vercel.app/login/signup) is open.
2. The username chosen must not already exist in the database.

Enter a valid, unique username in the "Username" field (e.g., admin_test12).
Enter a strong password in the "Password" field.
Enter the exact same password in the "Confirm Password" field.
Click on the "Create Account" button.
The account is successfully created. The system routes the user to the admin dashboard or a success confirmation screen, and a new admin record is provisioned in the database.
Verify that registration fails if the username is less than 3 characters long.
The LoadTrack signup page is open.

Enter a 2-character username (e.g., ad) in the "Username" field.
Enter a valid password in the "Password" field and confirm it.
Click on the "Create Account" button.
Account creation is blocked. An inline validation error message appears stating that the username must be between 3 and 50 characters.
Verify that registration fails if the username contains forbidden special characters (e.g., @, #, $).
The LoadTrack signup page is open.

Enter a username containing unallowed characters (e.g., admin@123) in the "Username" field.
Enter a valid password in the "Password" field and confirm it.
Click on the "Create Account" button.
Account creation is blocked. The UI displays a validation message emphasizing that only letters, numbers, dots, hyphens, and underscores are allowed.
Verify that the system prevents registration if the "Password" and "Confirm Password" fields do not match.
The LoadTrack signup page is open.

Enter a valid username in the "Username" field.
Enter SecurePass123 in the "Password" field.
Enter SecurePass124 in the "Confirm Password" field.
Click on the "Create Account" button.
Account creation fails. A clear error message is displayed (e.g., "Passwords do not match"), and the "Create Account" submission is halted.
Verify that registration is blocked if any required fields (marked with *) are left empty.
The LoadTrack signup page is open.

Leave all fields completely blank.
Click on the "Create Account" button.
The form is not submitted. Form fields are highlighted in red with individual error messages pointing out that Username and Password are required.
Verify that the visibility icon (eye icon) toggles the password text masking correctly.
The LoadTrack signup page is open.

Type a password into the "Password" field (text should initially appear masked as dots/asterisks).
Click the eye icon on the right side of the input field.
Observe the text format, then click it again.
Clicking the eye icon unmasks the password, revealing the plain text string. Clicking it a second time successfully masks the text again.
Login as ADMIN with valid credentials.

1. Open /login.
2. Enter admin username and password.
3. Submit login.
JWT is stored, role is ADMIN, and user lands on /app/home.
Login as DRIVER and DEALER routes to respective portals.
Active driver and dealer logins exist.

1. Login as driver.
2. Observe landing page.
3. Logout and login as dealer.
Driver reaches /app/driver; dealer reaches /app/dealer or dealer request/payment area per navigation.

1. Open login.
2. Enter valid username and wrong password.
3. Submit.
API returns 401 with invalid username/password message; no token is stored.
Forgot password resets a user's password to temporary value.

1. Open forgot-password.
2. Submit username.
3. Login using Loadtrack@123.
Reset succeeds and user can authenticate with temporary password.
Change password rejects incorrect current password.

1. Enter wrong current password.
2. Enter valid new and confirm password.
3. Submit.
API returns an error; old password remains valid.
Change password succeeds and logs out user.

1. Enter correct current password.
2. Enter matching new password.
3. Submit.
4. Attempt to use old token.
User is logged out; old password/token no longer gives access; new password works.
Protected API without token is blocked.

1. Navigate to /app/trucks.
2. Call GET /api/trucks with driver JWT.
UI guard blocks navigation or redirects; API returns 403.
Sand type read is allowed to all authenticated roles but mutation is admin-only.
Admin, driver, and dealer users exist.

1. GET /api/sand-types as each role.
2. POST /api/sand-types as driver/dealer.
GET succeeds for all roles; mutation returns 403 for driver/dealer.

1. Open Trucks.
2. Add truck with unique number, model, capacity, insurance, RC.
3. Save.
Truck is saved and listed with AVAILABLE status when status is omitted.
Truck form validates mandatory fields and capacity.

1. Open Add Truck.
2. Leave truck number/model blank.
3. Enter capacity 0.
4. Submit.
Validation prevents save and shows required/capacity errors.

1. Add another truck with truck number LT-1001.
2. Submit.
API returns 409 duplicate truck number message.
Truck list supports status and search filters.
At least three trucks exist with different statuses.

1. Filter by AVAILABLE.
2. Search by truck number fragment.
3. Move across pages.
Only matching records display; paginator counts update correctly.
Truck referenced by trip cannot be deleted.
Truck has at least one trip.

1. Attempt to delete referenced truck.
2. Confirm delete.
Delete is blocked with friendly FK-related message.
Available truck, driver, dealer, sand type, and settings exist.

1. Create trip using available truck.
2. Check truck status.
3. Mark trip COMPLETED.
Truck changes to ON_TRIP after trip creation and AVAILABLE after completion.
Create a driver and auto-generate login.
Admin is logged in; phone is unique.

1. Add driver with name, 10-digit phone, license, address, salary.
2. Save.
Driver is saved; response/UI shows generated DRIVER login with temporary password.
Driver phone and salary validations are enforced.

1. Add driver with 9-digit phone.
2. Enter negative salary.
3. Submit.
Validation errors are shown and no driver is created.

1. Add another driver with DL-100.
2. Submit.
Driver login can be retrieved or created from driver list.

1. Open driver actions.
2. Use login info/create login action.
System returns existing or newly created login details for the driver role.
Driver referenced by trips cannot be deleted.
Driver has at least one trip.

1. Attempt to delete driver.
2. Confirm delete.
Delete is blocked with friendly trip-reference message.
Create a dealer and auto-generate login.
Admin is logged in; phone is unique.

1. Add dealer with name, phone, address.
2. Save.
Dealer is saved; response/UI shows generated DEALER login with temporary password.

1. Add dealer with non-10-digit phone.
2. Submit.
Validation error is shown and no dealer is created.

1. Search by dealer name/phone fragment.
2. Change page size/page.
Only matching dealers appear and paginator reflects total results.
Dealer referenced by trips/payments cannot be deleted.
Dealer has at least one trip/payment.

1. Attempt to delete dealer.
2. Confirm delete.
Delete is blocked with friendly reference message.

1. Login as admin.
2. Open Sand Types.
3. Review catalog.
Fine, Medium, and Rough are available or can be confirmed as seeded defaults.
Admin creates/updates sand type with valid price.

1. Add a sand type with unique name and positive price.
2. Update price.
3. Save.
Catalog reflects new name/price; zero or negative price is rejected.
Historical trip total keeps rate snapshot after price change.
Existing trip uses sand type at old price.

1. Record trip total.
2. Change sand type price.
3. Reopen old trip and payment.
Old trip total remains unchanged; new trips use new price.
Settings are created or updated by one save action.

1. Open Settings.
2. Enter interest rate 2 and allowed days 7.
3. Save.
4. Edit values and save again.
First save creates settings; later save updates the same settings record.

1. Enter interest rate -1.
2. Enter allowed days 0.
3. Submit.
Validation blocks save with non-negative/minimum allowed-days errors.
Create trip and verify computed values.
Admin logged in; available truck, driver, dealer, sand type, settings exist.

1. Create trip with 12 tons and sand rate 1800.
2. Save.
3. Open trip details.
Trip is PENDING; rate is snapshotted; total amount is 21600.

1. Create trip with trip date 2026-06-01 and allowed days 7.
2. Open Payments.
Payment exists with PENDING status, paid amount 0, original/final amount equal trip total, due date 2026-06-08.
Unavailable truck cannot be assigned to another trip.

1. Create another trip using the same truck.
2. Submit.
System rejects with 'truck is not AVAILABLE' message.
Pending trip edit recomputes payment before payment starts.

1. Edit trip tons or sand type.
2. Save.
3. Open payment.
Trip total, payment original/final amount, and due date are recalculated.
Trip edit is blocked after payment starts.
Trip payment is PARTIAL or PAID.
System rejects edit with 'Cannot edit trip after payment has started'.

1. Change status to STARTED.
2. Change status to COMPLETED.
Both transitions succeed and truck is AVAILABLE on COMPLETED.
Invalid trip status transition is rejected.
1. Attempt to change status back to STARTED or PENDING.
Trip list filters by status, date, driver, dealer, truck.

1. Apply each filter alone.
2. Combine date range and dealer.
3. Change pagination.
Only matching trips appear; filters are sent to backend query parameters.
Deleting trip frees ON_TRIP truck when allowed.
Trip is removed and truck becomes AVAILABLE.
Payments exist in PENDING, PARTIAL, and PAID states.

1. Filter by dealer.
2. Filter by status.
3. Enable overdueOnly.
Only matching payments appear and pagination remains accurate.
Interest is zero before due date.
Payment due date is today or future.
Interest is 0; final amount equals original amount.
Interest is calculated for overdue open payment.
Settings interest is 2%; payment original is 20000 and due date is before today.
Interest is 400.00 and final amount is 20400.00.
Partial installment creates transaction and PARTIAL status.

1. Mark paid with amount 5000.
2. Reopen payment/receipt data.
Paid amount is 5000, status is PARTIAL, and a transaction row is recorded.
Final installment marks payment PAID and snapshots interest.
Payment is PARTIAL with remaining balance.

1. Pay exact remaining balance.
2. Change date/settings if possible.
3. Reopen payment.
Payment status is PAID; payment date set; interest/final amount remain locked.
Open payment has known remaining balance.

1. Enter paid amount greater than final amount due.
2. Submit.
System rejects with clear overpayment amount and does not record transaction.
Already paid payment cannot be paid again.
System rejects with payment already fully paid message.
Admin downloads receipt after at least one transaction.
Payment has at least one installment.

1. Open Payments.
2. Click receipt/download for payment.
PDF downloads with receipt number, dealer, trip, payment, and installment details.
Receipt generation before transaction is blocked.
System rejects or disables receipt download until transaction exists.
Dealer has own paid/partial payment with transaction.

1. Login as dealer.
2. Download own receipt.
3. Attempt another dealer's payment receipt via URL.
Own receipt succeeds; cross-dealer access is rejected.
Receipt PDF is generated without persistent filesystem dependency.

1. Download receipt.
2. Repeat after app restart or clean temp area if possible.
Receipt bytes are returned from API without relying on a saved local file.
Dealer submits a valid trip request.
Dealer logged in; sand types exist.

1. Open Dealer Requests.
2. Select sand type, tons, pickup, delivery, requested date, notes.
3. Submit.
Request is created with PENDING status and estimated amount shown from current rate.
Dealer request validation blocks missing or invalid data.

1. Leave sand type blank.
2. Enter tons 0.
3. Submit.
Validation blocks request and shows required/min errors.

1. Click Cancel.
2. Confirm.
3. Refresh request list.
Request status becomes CANCELLED and action is no longer available.
Admin lists and filters dealer requests with pending count.
At least one request in each status exists.

1. Login as admin.
2. Open Trip Requests.
3. Filter by PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED.
4. Check sidebar badge.
Filtered list and pending badge match backend counts.
Pending request exists; available truck and driver exist.

1. Open pending request.
2. Select truck and driver.
3. Approve.
Request becomes APPROVED, approved trip ID is linked, trip/payment are created, truck is ON_TRIP.
Admin cannot approve request with unavailable truck.
Pending request exists; selected truck is ON_TRIP.
System rejects with 'truck is not AVAILABLE' message and request remains PENDING.
Admin rejects pending request with mandatory reason.

1. Click Reject.
2. Submit empty reason.
3. Submit valid reason.
Empty reason is blocked; valid reason sets status REJECTED and saves admin notes.
Driver dashboard metrics are scoped to logged-in driver.
Driver has trips this month and other drivers also have trips.

1. Login as driver.
2. Open /app/driver.
3. Compare dashboard totals to driver's trips.
Totals include only logged-in driver's trips, tons, and salary.
Driver trip list status filters work.

1. Click status filter chips.
2. Review list.
Only logged-in driver's matching trips appear.

1. Open /app/payments and /app/dealer.
2. Call dealer portal API with driver JWT.
Dealer dashboard metrics are scoped to logged-in dealer.
Dealer has payments; another dealer has payments.

1. Login as dealer.
2. Open /app/dealer.
3. Compare balances and overdue count.
Metrics include only logged-in dealer data.
Dealer payment list status and overdue filters work.
Only the dealer's matching payments appear.
Dealer cannot access other dealers' data.
Dealer is logged in; another dealer has known payment ID.

1. Attempt direct API URL for another dealer's receipt or payment.
2. Attempt admin payments URL.
Admin dashboard cards match source data.
Admin has seeded/created trucks, drivers, dealers, trips, payments.

1. Open /app/home.
2. Compare KPI cards against database/API counts.
Total trucks, available/on-trip, drivers, dealers, trips, earnings, and outstanding values match backend summary.
Dashboard charts render from summary endpoint.
Dashboard summary endpoint has monthly/status data.

1. Open /app/home.
2. Inspect bar and doughnut charts.
Last-6-month earnings and trip status distribution charts render with nonblank data when records exist.
Trips report filters return correct rows.
Trips exist across date ranges, trucks, drivers, dealers, statuses.

1. Open Reports.
2. Select Trips report.
3. Apply each filter and combinations.
Rows match selected filters and totals reflect filtered rows.
Payments report filters return correct rows.
Payments exist across date ranges, dealers, statuses, overdue states.

1. Select Payments report.
2. Apply dealer/status/date/overdue filters.
Trips report exports to PDF and XLSX.

1. Apply a trips filter.
2. Export PDF.
3. Export XLSX.
4. Open files.
PDF and Excel contain the same filtered data, readable headers, and totals/currency values.
Payments report exports to PDF and XLSX.

1. Apply a payments filter.
2. Export PDF.
3. Export XLSX.
4. Open files.
Exports contain filtered payment rows, amount fields, status, due dates, and totals.
Account page loads current user context.
Admin, driver, and dealer users exist.
Account screen loads for every authenticated role and identifies current user context.
Logged in user is on Account page.

1. Enter correct current password.
2. Enter different new/confirm values.
3. Submit.
UI blocks submission with mismatch error.
Swagger UI and OpenAPI docs are public.
Both endpoints load without JWT and show controllers/schemas.
Validation errors are structured and user-readable.

1. Submit invalid DTOs for truck, driver, trip, payment.
2. Inspect UI/API response.
API returns 400 with field errors; frontend shows clear messages.

1. Set browser width to 360px.
2. Visit dashboard, lists, forms, and portals.
Sidebar overlays, tables scroll horizontally inside containers, and no full-page horizontal scroll appears.
